unavailable.title: Connections for AI apps are off
unavailable.body: An administrator hasn't turned on the MCP server (Settings → AI), or your role doesn't allow connecting AI apps. Connections you already have are listed below: while the MCP server is off they are paused, not revoked — revoke any you no longer want.

oauth.title: This instance uses OAuth sign-in
oauth.body: It is served over HTTPS, so AI apps sign in through your browser: lazyit shows a consent screen where you choose what the app may do. There is no token to copy.
oauth.cloudConnectors: Cloud connectors (claude.ai, ChatGPT) connect from the provider's servers, so they work only if this instance is reachable from the internet over HTTPS. Desktop and command-line apps (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code) only need to reach it from your computer.
oauth.internalCa: If this instance's certificate comes from an internal certificate authority, tell Claude Code (and other Node.js-based apps) to trust it before starting them: export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/internal-ca.pem.
oauth.viewingOverHttp: You opened this page over plain HTTP. AI apps must use this instance's HTTPS address.

personalToken.title: This instance uses personal tokens
personalToken.plainHttp: It is served over plain HTTP (LAN mode). OAuth sign-in needs HTTPS — sign-in codes and tokens must not cross the network unencrypted, and AI apps refuse to sign in over plain HTTP — so it is off here. Instead, create a personal token below and give it to your AI app.
personalToken.httpsNotConfigured: You're on HTTPS, but the instance isn't configured with an HTTPS address (an administrator sets it with WEB_ORIGIN), so OAuth sign-in stays off and AI apps connect with a personal token you create below.
personalToken.cloudConnectors: Cloud connectors (claude.ai, ChatGPT) can't be used: they connect from the provider's servers and need a publicly reachable HTTPS instance. Desktop and command-line apps on your network work.
personalToken.handleWithCare: A personal token acts as you until it expires or you revoke it. Treat it like a password, give it the shortest useful expiry, and keep it out of shared files.

claudeCode.title: Install in Claude Code
claudeCode.description: The lazyit plugin gives Claude Code the lazyit skill — what lazyit is and how to use it — and connects it to this instance's MCP server in one step.

oauth.stepInstall: Add this instance's plugin marketplace and install the plugin:
oauth.stepSignIn: Start Claude Code and run /mcp, choose lazyit and sign in. Your browser opens lazyit's consent screen.
oauth.stepUpdates: Updates aren't automatic by default. To receive new versions of the skill, open /plugin in Claude Code, go to Marketplaces, select {marketplace} and enable auto-update.

personalToken.noMarketplace: The one-command install needs HTTPS, so on this instance install the plugin from a download:

manual.title: Install from a download
manual.stepDownload: Download the plugin. It is built for this instance and contains no token.
manual.stepUnzip: Unzip it into your Claude Code skills folder. Claude Code loads it as the plugin lazyit@skills-dir in your next session:
manual.tryOnce: To try it for one session without installing, run {command} instead.
manual.stepSignInOauth: Start Claude Code and run /mcp to sign in.
manual.stepToken: Create a personal token below. Claude Code asks for it when you enable the plugin and keeps it in your system's keychain — it is never stored in the plugin files.

errors.originUnknown: The instance doesn't know its own address, so the plugin can't be built. An administrator needs to set the instance's public address (WEB_ORIGIN).
errors.unavailable: The plugin isn't available: connections for AI apps were turned off.

AI_DISABLED.title: Connections for AI apps are off
AI_DISABLED.body: An administrator hasn't turned on the MCP server on this instance, so no app can be authorized right now.

FORBIDDEN.title: Your account can't connect AI apps
FORBIDDEN.body: Authorizing an AI app needs the “Connect external AI agents (MCP)” permission (ai:connect). Ask an administrator if you need it.

INVALID_CLIENT.title: This app isn't allowed
INVALID_CLIENT.body: The app isn't registered with this instance, or your administrator no longer allows it. Start the connection again from the app, or ask your administrator.

INVALID_REDIRECT.title: This request can't be trusted
INVALID_REDIRECT.body: The app asked to send you to an address it didn't register. For your safety lazyit won't send you anywhere. Start the connection again from the app.

unavailable.title: App sign-in isn't available here
unavailable.body: OAuth sign-in for AI apps needs this instance to be served over HTTPS with its address configured. On a plain-HTTP (LAN) instance, connect AI apps with a personal token instead.

invalidRequest.title: This sign-in link is incomplete
invalidRequest.body: The authorization request is missing information or is malformed. Start the connection again from your app.

clientError.title: The app sent an invalid request
clientError.body: lazyit can't continue with this request. You can return to the app so it can show you the error.

unsafeRedirect.title: Unexpected response
unsafeRedirect.body: lazyit received a return address that doesn't match the app's, so it won't send you there. Start the connection again from the app.

unknown.title: Something went wrong
unknown.body: lazyit couldn't process this authorization request. Try again from your app.
